editorial.evidence: Read all 48 captured sections of the chatbot platform source and rewrote them into the five-section shell. Tutorial parts 1-8 became eight walkthrough steps; the quadratic-history and unit-cost material, records/endpoints, the turn-handler code, three of the four failure drills with the pytest boundary tests, and the Item 17/18 coverage-notes gaps became five deep dives. The worksheet and model answer are interleaved in Practice so each worksheet prompt precedes its model-answer reveal; the four mock prompts had no source answers, so their reveals are assembled from the case and labelled as worked examples, as is the users-and-workflows answer. Repetition consolidated: the 60-second version, key takeaways and the answer-key architecture restate the walkthrough, so they map to existing passages rather than repeating. Added definitions (egress, live permissions, SSO, ACL, TTFT, DLP, works council, query-time resolvable, legal hold, SLO, p95, RPO, SSE, fail closed, game day) and arithmetic steps (57,600/hour, 40x41/2=820, 4.6M/320/6,400). Invented figures (board/on-call quotes, impact statement) keep the source's invented label; $22 keeps the beta-measurement caveat. Source inconsistencies resolved in text (2026-11-16): answer key's week 0-8 rollout vs the tutorial's weeks 1-23+ phases → the four-phase schedule (Alpha 1-6, Beta 7-14, GA 15-22, assistants 23+), because the phase table, the phases figure and the 'plain chat within six weeks' decision all use it; worksheet's 'one corpus' → 'the first corpora', matching the Beta's two corpora.
